titleEn: Sheep Sleep in the Dark Too!

pages.text: "Mom, do not put out the lamp!" Pipo pulled the covers to his nose. Outside the round window, one yard lamp burned. All the sheep were already in the pen.
Mom blew out the lamp. The round window darkened, leaving faint moonlight. Pipo's heart thumped. "I do not like the dark..." He wanted to sleep with the lamp on.
On the wall—oh? A long, swaying shadow! It looked like a scary snake. "Oh... what is that?" He squeezed his eyes shut and trembled.
Hearing little sobs, Mom entered quietly. "Pipo, that scared you. It is all right." Sitting beside his bed, she held his hand. Hers was warm.
"What scared you?" He pointed. "There... a snake." Mom guided his hand to the peg beside the shadow. Soft—the shadow belonged to his hanging scarf! "Not a snake?"
Mom lifted him before the round window. The pen outside was dark; inside, sheep slept leaning against each other. She whispered, "Look, sheep sleep in the dark too!"
Now Pipo touched what made each shadow. Round meant wooden ball, pointed meant bedpost. Feeling them one by one left nothing scary. "Sheep sleep in the dark too!"
His heart no longer raced. "Dark just means the lamp is off!" He crouched on the covers, hands at his chest. His chest grew warm.
Mom opened fingers one by one. "One, say you are scared! Two, touch each thing with your hand! Three, look at the sheep outside!" Pipo nodded.
Mom hugged him and patted his back. "It is all right to feel scared. Mom is beside you." Dark just meant the lamp was out. Closing his eyes, he whispered, "Sheep sleep in the dark too!"
